answer_key_policy.leak_closed: The per-episode repair_ops.json next to each fault.kicad_sch IS the ground-truth repair and is deliberately NOT part of the task input exposed to a solving arm. tools.repairbench copies only fault.kicad_sch into the arm workspace.
answer_key_policy.why_this_matters: Before this benchmark existed, repair_ops.json sat in the same directory as the fault schematic, so any arm given the fixture directory could read the answer. That is an answer leak, not a benchmark.

metric_layers.primary_oracle: target rule FAIL -> PASS under the netlist-scope contract
metric_layers.regression_guard: every non-target rule that was PASS before the attempt must still be PASS after it
metric_layers.structural_preservation: secondary; the post-repair netlist must match tests/fixtures/repair_pr1/private/acceptance_v1.json for the episode

episodes.title: USB D+/D- net labels mislabelled at the module pins
episodes.fault_summary: Series resistors exist but the nets at U1.13/U1.14 are not USB_DM/USB_DP, so the module side of the USB pair is unlabelled/misassigned.

episodes.title: SHT30 ADDR pin left floating
episodes.fault_summary: U2.2 (ADDR) is on an unnamed net instead of GND, so the sensor address is undefined.

episodes.title: USB series termination resistors missing
episodes.fault_summary: R7/R8 (22R USB series) are absent, so the USB_DP_CONN / USB_DM_CONN to USB_DP / USB_DM chain is broken.

episodes.title: GPIO9 boot-strap pull-up missing
episodes.fault_summary: R9 (10k +3V3 -> BOOT) is absent, so the boot strap has no defined high level.

episodes.title: EN reset network capacitor missing
episodes.fault_summary: C5 (1uF EN -> GND) is absent, so the EN pin has no approved reset network.

controls.noop: Do nothing. MUST leave every episode's target rule failing. If a no-op episode scores PASS the benchmark is broken and results must be discarded.
controls.oracle: Apply the withheld repair_ops.json. Every episode MUST reach primary PASS. If an oracle episode fails, the fixture or the contract projection is inconsistent and results must be discarded.
controls.why_both: A benchmark that a do-nothing arm passes measures nothing; a benchmark whose answer key does not reach PASS is unsolvable. Both controls are required before any arm result is reportable.

limitations: v0.1 has 5 episodes drawn from a single board (M2). ADR-023 asks for 20-30 across 3-5 fault families; v0.1 is a scope-and-harness rehearsal, not the final benchmark.
The oracle is the netlist-scope projection of the M2 contract, which is WEAKER than the parent contract (no intent/pcb/firmware assertions). See derivation.known_loss_of_power in the contract file.
Schematic-only episodes: no PCB, no ERC/DRC, no KiCad invocation, no firmware constant check.

No ground truth about whether a repair is the one a human would choose. The contract pins the net-level intent; multiple valid repairs may satisfy it, and structural agreement with acceptance_v1.json is the secondary guard, not a proof of optimality.
